data: This course introduces ancient civilizations, specifically focusing on the Indus Valley with discussions on Mesopotamia, Egypt, and China, and an overview of developments in other regions of Asia, Africa, and the Americas. We discuss alternate theories regarding urbanisation and definitions of civilizations. We also highlight discoveries and theoretical and methodological approaches in archaeology that have influenced interpretations of diverse civilizations. The course highlights transformations from early agro-pastoral Neolithic cultures with an emphasis on examining cultural transitions, the origins of agriculture, and the spread of domesticated plants and animals. We discuss the influence of environmental changes on the rise, spread, and decline of civilizations. We highlight issues related to the diverse manifestations of settlements, urban architecture and spatial organisation, governance, socio-economic structures, intellectual and religious lives, technologies, architecture, literature, art/craft, and more. The course discusses ancient population migrations as inferred from archaeological, linguistic, and genetic studies. It concludes by situating ancient worlds within modern contexts as related to changing perceptions and constructions of the past.
